dataset_identity.row_meaning: Individual sales transaction (purchase) at a store or online
health_observations: Date stored as string, may need parsing to proper datetime
misinterpretation_risks: IsReturned occurs after purchase; using it as a predictor for pre‑purchase behavior creates leakage
Assuming Age missingness is random can bias demographic analyses
StoreLocation may conflate physical and online sales, leading to misleading geographic insights
FeedbackScore can be influenced by return status, causing target leakage if both are used together
TransactionID is an arbitrary identifier and should never be used as a predictive feature

user_intent.decision_supported: Identify high‑risk return transactions so the business can allocate resources, adjust inventory, and intervene with customers before shipment
constraints: Avoid using post‑purchase variables (e.g., FeedbackScore) that cause target leakage
Handle missing Age values appropriately (not assume MCAR)
Treat extreme Amount outliers to prevent model distortion
Parse Date string to proper datetime for temporal features
Exclude TransactionID and any identifier columns from features

modifications.problem: Date stored as string, not datetime
modifications.impact: Prevents accurate temporal ordering, time‑based feature engineering (e.g., day of week, month) and correct handling of time gaps in analysis.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Parse the Date column to pandas datetime with errors='coerce', then drop rows where parsing fails (expected <0.5% of rows).
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Leave as string (limits temporal features); convert to ordinal integer without proper parsing (risk of incorrect ordering).
modifications.effect: All 100% of rows have Date type converted to datetime; up to 0.5% rows may be removed.

modifications.impact: Age is a key demographic variable; missingness can bias segment analyses and any model that uses age as a feature.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Age with the median age within each Gender group; if Gender itself is missing, use the overall median age.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Row deletion (would lose 20% of data); simple overall mean imputation (ignores gender differences); complex predictive regression imputation (unnecessary complexity and risk of over‑fit).
modifications.effect: Age values for ~20% of rows are filled; column remains float64.

modifications.problem: 10% missing Amount values and extreme outliers
modifications.impact: Amount drives revenue calculations and model targets; outliers can distort statistics and impede model convergence.
modifications.strategy_chosen: First apply winsorization at the 1st and 99th percentiles to cap extreme values, then impute missing Amount with the median of the winsorized, non‑missing amounts.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Dropping rows (loss of 10% of transactions); mean imputation (sensitive to outliers); building a predictive model for Amount (adds unnecessary complexity).
modifications.effect: All rows retain an Amount value; outliers are capped; missing values for ~10% of rows are filled with the winsorized median.

modifications.impact: FeedbackScore gauges customer satisfaction; missingness can bias average ratings and downstream sentiment analyses.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing FeedbackScore with the median score of the corresponding ProductCategory; if the category is missing, fall back to the overall median score.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Row removal (10% loss); overall median imputation (ignores product‑specific rating patterns); predictive modeling for scores (excessive complexity).
modifications.effect: FeedbackScore for ~10% of rows is populated; column remains float64.

All restricted identifiers remain untouched, ensuring integrity of primary/foreign key relationships.
